minutes.headline: Commission pushed a wetland-crossing home design to relocate outside the buffer, then continued every open case to June 17
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission worked through a full agenda of septic, driveway, substation and home-construction wetland filings, continuing nearly all of them to June 17 while pressing the West Townsend Road applicant to move a proposed house outside the wetland buffer and add planting and staging plans. It also approved a lake herbicide treatment and a cleaning quote for the town's Hollis Road property, heard that mosquito-control funding may have been cut from the town budget, and got updates on two open enforcement cases and an upcoming FY26/FY27 conservation budget.

what_happened.line: Commission pressed a proposed West Townsend Road home to relocate outside the wetland buffer and required planting, replication and staging plans before its next hearing.
Five other pending filings, including a failed septic system, two common driveways and a Unitil substation, were all continued to June 17 rather than decided.
Commission approved a herbicide treatment plan for Hickory Hills Lake and a cleaning quote for the town's Hollis Road property, with one member abstaining on the cleaning vote.
Commissioners said mosquito-control program funding may have been cut from the town's balanced budget, though nobody was certain.
An enforcement matter at 1168 Mass Ave will stay open with no continuance date set while state and federal reviews continue.

why_it_matters: The West Townsend Road relocation and added planting/staging conditions affect where and how a home gets built near a wetland, and add steps before construction can proceed.
The mosquito-control funding question, if confirmed, would affect a service the town has relied on for pest control across the community.
The Hickory Hills Lake treatment and Hollis Road cleaning are town-funded actions on a public waterbody and a town-owned building, both now moving forward.
watch_next: June 17, 2026 Conservation Commission meeting: continued hearings resume and an FY26/FY27 conservation budget vote is expected.
